complete_examples.text: Article An advanced vehicle–slab track interaction model considering rail random irregularities Lei Xu1, Zhaowei Chen2 and Wanming Zhai1 Abstract This paper investigates a more advanced vertical vehicle–slab track interaction model (VTIM) by considering the discontinuity of track slabs, besides, it can be degenerated to the traditional two-dimensional model conveniently.
However, the discontinuity between adjacent track slabs for mitigating the thermal expansion effects was neglected.
Besides, it has shown that the longitudinal unevenness of the track support stiffness has significant influence on the plasticity of track slabs.

However, the residual deformation caused by the plasticity of track slabs will affect the geometric status of the tracks, and sometimes, lead to crack, void, and plastic damage of track slabs and even influence the running performance of the train.

With the wide usage of the precast and bi-directional prestress track slabs, the damages that appeared in the concrete track slab and basement is generally rare, and mostly formed on the surface [1] that causes rather limited influence ∗Corresponding author.
CZMs have obtained intensive attention for the last two decades and have been employed in railway track filed to predict the interlaminar failure between track slabs and filling layers.
